morphology_keys.life_cycle: Perennial in the Williamson County treatment; broader treatments note substantial variation.
morphology_keys.habit: Twining or trailing vine with a taproot and long lateral roots.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate; ovate-deltoid to shallowly 3-lobed, cordate at base; leaf shape variable.
morphology_keys.sepals: Outer sepals about 8–11 mm, usually ciliate/hairy; inner sepals about 10–12 mm.
morphology_keys.corolla: Pink to purple, usually about 2.5–4.5 cm, darker in the throat.
morphology_keys.key: Shorter, broader sepals than I. hederacea; perennial rooting habit also helps.

taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Ipomoea cordatotriloba at species rank. ITIS/GRIN still recognize the autonym var. cordatotriloba as an infraspecific treatment, while Kew folds var. torreyana into the species. For the learner, the Hays source row 'Ipomoea cordatotriloba var. cordatotriloba' is represented inside this canonical species page rather than duplicated.
synonyms: Ipomoea cordatotriloba var. cordatotriloba (source/infraspecific treatment represented in this species card)
Ipomoea cordatotriloba var. torreyana (A.Gray) D.F.Austin (Kew synonym of I. cordatotriloba)

infraspecific_lesson.Ipomoea cordatotriloba var. cordatotrilo: Legacy/current-source autonym used by ITIS/GRIN and local source lists. The learner maps it to this species-level card so the same biological concept is not duplicated.
infraspecific_lesson.Ipomoea cordatotriloba var. torreyana: Current Kew/POWO treats this name as a synonym of Ipomoea cordatotriloba.

field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: Use the flower and sepals together: a medium 20–38 mm corolla with 8–14 mm lanceolate-to-ovate sepals, then use perennial habit and pubescence as support.
fastest_traits: Sepals 8–14 mm; outer sepals narrower than inner
Leaves cordate to 3–5(–7)-lobed and too variable to identify alone
Typical var. cordatotriloba is hairy/ciliate; var. torreyana can be glabrous

look_alikes.distinction: I. triloba usually has a 10–20 mm corolla and 6–7 mm sepals; I. cordatotriloba is typically larger in both, although boundaries can approach.
I. hederacea has much more exaggerated long distal sepal portions, abruptly narrowed from a broader base.
I. lacunosa usually has a small white 15–20(–25) mm corolla and glabrous acuminate sepals; intermediate plants require attention to the I. ×leucantha hybrid possibility.

hybrid_caution.note: FNA reports this hybrid from I. lacunosa × I. cordatotriloba in the southeastern United States. Intermediate small white/lavender plants should not be forced from leaf shape alone.

diagnostic_photo_targets: Same-scale flower side view beside I. triloba
Outer and inner sepals with ruler
Multiple leaves from one plant to teach variability
Perennial/rootstock or basal habit context when visible
